report.summary: Reviewed chunk 1 of subprocess_adapter.py; claims checked, several broken/uncheckable.
risks: line 211 | high | prompt_mode='stdin' without stdin_prompt_marker: prompt is silently dropped, contradicting docstring 'prompt_mode: stdin' | add a check that marker exists when prompt_mode is stdin and prompt is non-empty
line 211 | medium | prompt_mode='none' with empty prompt is allowed, but create_session contract says 'does not accept a prompt' | decide whether empty prompt is acceptable and document
line 211 | high | prompt_mode='stdin' with close_stdin_after_prompt=True: process may exit before events are read; resume/streaming semantics unclear | trace event loop after stdin close
line 211 | medium | prompt passed as argument when prompt_mode='argument' and prompt contains spaces: single argv element, may be misparsed by CLI | confirm CLI argument contract
line 211 | medium | prompt_mode='stdin' with stdin_prompt_marker but no prompt: marker appended with no prompt, process may hang | verify CLI behavior with empty stdin
line 211 | low | env merge order: user env overrides os.environ, but no validation of env keys | confirm intended precedence
line 211 | low | cwd_arg and model_arg are appended after default_args but before extra_args; if default_args already contain positional, order may break | verify CLI arg parsing
line 211 | low | session_id uses command stem, not runtime_name; collisions possible if same command used with different profiles | consider including runtime_name
line 211 | low | timeout_s is stored but never enforced in this chunk; no watchdog task created | trace timeout enforcement in chunk 2
line 211 | low | _publish uses self._sessions[session_id] unguarded; if session is removed before publish, KeyError | consider using .get

claims.text: This is a process/event normalization layer, not a universal agent protocol
claims.why: The code is explicitly configured, non-interactive, with built-in profiles; it does not attempt universal protocol.

claims.text: each CLI still needs a verified command profile and provider-specific event parser
claims.why: The code requires RuntimeConfig and profiles are limited; event parsing is not shown here.

claims.text: Built-in profiles are limited to CLIs whose local --help contract is exercised by tests
claims.why: No tests visible in this chunk; cannot verify --help contract.

claims.text: Verified process-launch contract for one CLI runtime
claims.why: The dataclass fields define command, args, streaming, etc., and is used to launch.

The comment claims output_format can be 'text', but this chunk never validates the value; the code treats it as opaque and never branches on it. An invalid value would be accepted silently, contradicting the comment's implied enum.
Type is Literal and default is 'argument'.

claims.text: These profiles describe one-shot, non-interactive invocations.
claims.why: The profiles use --print, exec, --ask-for-approval never, etc., consistent with one-shot non-interactive.

claims.text: Antigravity isn't listed: no agy executable or stable JSON protocol exists on this machine, and a desktop/IDE session does not imply a callable CLI contract.
claims.why: Cannot verify existence of agy executable or machine state from this chunk.

claims.text: Run a configured CLI in a bounded working directory and normalize output.
claims.why: create_session launches process in a resolved cwd; output normalization is not in this chunk but the launch is bounded.

claims.text: Either config or command must be provided
claims.why: If config is None and command is falsy, raises ValueError.
If root.is_dir() is false, raises ValueError.

claims.text: Unknown or unverified runtime ... Pass an explicit RuntimeConfig for a custom CLI.
claims.why: Raises ValueError with message listing profiles and suggesting explicit config.

claims.text: session cwd is not a directory
claims.why: If cwd.is_dir() is false, raises ValueError.
If model is provided and model_arg is None, raises ValueError.

claims.text: profile does not accept a prompt
claims.why: The error is raised only when prompt is truthy and prompt_mode is 'none'. If prompt is empty (falsy), no error is raised, so a session is created with an empty prompt even though the profile 'does not accept a prompt'. The claim 'does not accept a prompt' is too broad; it only rejects non-empty prompts.

claims.text: session not found or stdin unavailable
claims.why: If session is None or stdin is None, raises RuntimeError with that message.
If is_closing() is true, raises RuntimeError with that message.
